title: Pinsker's inequality
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and let $\mathrm{TV}(\mu,
u)$ denote their total variation distance and $\mathrm{KL}(\mu\,\|\,
u)$ their Kullback–Leibler divergence. Then
\[
  2\,\mathrm{TV}(\mu,
u)^2 \;\le\; \mathrm{KL}(\mu\,\|\,
u),
\]
where the left-hand side is regarded as an element of the extended nonnegative reals $[0,\infty]$.
hypotheses_covered: μ is a probability measure on Ω
ν is a probability measure on Ω
replaced:
For any two probability measures $\mu$ and $\nu$ on $\Omega$,
\[
  \mathrm{ofReal}\bigl(2\,\mathrm{TV}(\mu,\nu)^2\bigr) \;\le\; \mathrm{KL}(\mu \| \nu),
\]
where the inequality is in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^\infty$ and KL divergence uses natural logarithms.
